title: On a Method of Investigating Periodicities in Disturbed Series, with Special Reference to Wolfer's Sunspot Numbers
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London. Series A
question: Can irregular cycles come from random shocks fed through a simple recursion?
changed: Introduced the autoregression: today's value as a linear function of past values plus noise.

title: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems
question: How do you estimate a hidden state recursively from noisy observations?
changed: The Kalman filter: a predict–update recursion that is the optimal linear estimator for linear Gaussian state-space models.
assumed: Linear dynamics and Gaussian noise with known covariances.

title: Maximum likelihood estimates of linear dynamic systems
question: Once all the data are in, what is the best estimate of each past state?
changed: The RTS smoother: a backward pass after the Kalman filter that uses future observations too.

title: Error bounds for convolutional codes and an asymptotically optimum decoding algorithm
question: How do you find the most likely hidden sequence without enumerating them all?
changed: Dynamic programming over a trellis finds the single most probable path in linear time.

title: A Maximization Technique Occurring in the Statistical Analysis of Probabilistic Functions of Markov Chains
question: How do you fit a hidden Markov model when the states are never observed?
changed: The Baum–Welch algorithm: forward–backward probabilities and an iteration that never decreases the likelihood.

title: Maximum Likelihood from Incomplete Data via the EM Algorithm
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B (Methodological)
question: Is there a general recipe for maximum likelihood with missing data?
changed: The EM algorithm: alternate expected complete-data likelihood and maximization; Baum–Welch is a special case.

title: On a measure of lack of fit in time series models
question: Are a fitted model's residuals white noise?
changed: The Ljung–Box portmanteau test of many autocorrelations at once, with better small-sample behavior than Box–Pierce.

title: Distribution of the Estimators for Autoregressive Time Series With a Unit Root
venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association
question: How do you test whether a series is a random walk?
changed: Under a unit root the usual t-statistic has a non-standard distribution; tabulated its critical values.

title: A Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Covariance Matrix Estimator and a Direct Test for Heteroskedasticity
question: How do you get honest standard errors when error variance isn't constant?
changed: The sandwich estimator: valid least-squares standard errors under heteroskedasticity of unknown form.

title: Macroeconomics and Reality
question: Can we learn from macro data without imposing incredible restrictions?
changed: Vector autoregressions and impulse responses: let the data speak through unrestricted dynamic systems.

title: Autoregressive Conditional Heteroscedasticity with Estimates of the Variance of United Kingdom Inflation
question: Can the variance of a series be forecast from its own recent shocks?
changed: ARCH: conditional variance as a function of past squared shocks, capturing volatility clustering.

title: Large Sample Properties of Generalized Method of Moments Estimators
question: How do you estimate a model defined only by moment conditions, like an Euler equation?
changed: GMM: consistent, asymptotically normal estimation from moment conditions, with an overidentification test.

title: Generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity
question: Can ARCH be made parsimonious?
changed: GARCH(1,1): lagged variance enters the recursion, so three parameters capture long volatility memory.
assumed: Symmetric response to good and bad news.

title: Co-Integration and Error Correction: Representation, Estimation, and Testing
question: What if two random walks share a long-run relation?
changed: Cointegration: a stationary combination of nonstationary series, with error-correction dynamics. The statistics of pairs trading.

title: A Simple, Positive Semi-Definite, Heteroskedasticity and Autocorrelation Consistent Covariance Matrix
question: How do you get standard errors when errors are also autocorrelated?
changed: Bartlett-weighted autocovariances give a HAC covariance that is always positive semi-definite.

title: A New Approach to the Economic Analysis of Nonstationary Time Series and the Business Cycle
question: Can a series switch between regimes that are never observed?
changed: Markov-switching models with a filter for regime probabilities: recessions found from GNP data alone.

title: Conditional Heteroskedasticity in Asset Returns: A New Approach
question: How do you let bad news raise volatility more than good news?
changed: EGARCH: model log variance with an asymmetric response, with no positivity constraints needed.

title: Estimation and Hypothesis Testing of Cointegration Vectors in Gaussian Vector Autoregressive Models
question: How many cointegrating relations does a system have?
changed: Maximum likelihood estimation and trace tests for the cointegration rank in a VAR.

title: On the Relation between the Expected Value and the Volatility of the Nominal Excess Return on Stocks
question: Are high-volatility periods rewarded with high expected returns?
changed: GJR-GARCH adds a term for negative shocks; with it, the risk–return relation turns negative.

title: Dynamic linear models with Markov-switching
question: How do you smooth regime probabilities, and combine switching with state-space models?
changed: The Kim filter and smoother: tractable approximate inference for Markov-switching state-space models.

title: Answering the Skeptics: Yes, Standard Volatility Models do Provide Accurate Forecasts
question: Why do GARCH forecasts score so badly against squared returns?
changed: Squared daily returns are a terribly noisy target; against intraday realized variance, GARCH forecasts are good.

title: International Asset Allocation With Regime Shifts
question: Do correlations jump in bear regimes, and does that kill diversification?
changed: Regime-switching allocation: correlations and volatilities rise together in bad regimes, yet international diversification still pays.

title: Dynamic Conditional Correlation
question: How do you model time-varying correlations for many assets?
changed: DCC: univariate GARCH for each variance, then a GARCH-like recursion for the correlation matrix.

title: Modeling and Forecasting Realized Volatility
question: What if volatility is measured from intraday data instead of estimated?
changed: Treat realized variance as observed and model it directly; it forecasts better than GARCH on daily data.

title: A Simple Approximate Long-Memory Model of Realized Volatility
question: Can long memory in volatility be captured with plain regression?
changed: HAR-RV: regress realized variance on its daily, weekly and monthly averages. Hard to beat.
